approved: Recycling and Waste Reduction Charges (Excise) Bill 2020
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill is part of a package of three Charges Bills that would let the Commonwealth recover the costs of regulating waste material exports.
The package would set up a framework for imposing charges, but the actual amounts and who pays them would be decided later in regulations made by the Governor-General.
Three separate Acts are needed because the Constitution requires excise, customs and other taxation to be in different Acts.
The Charges Bills would enable the Commonwealth to recover regulatory costs for waste material exports.
The package would provide a framework for imposing charges, with amounts set by future regulations.
The bills would ensure cost recovery mechanisms are in place for Commonwealth services related to regulated waste material.
Exporters of regulated waste material and the Commonwealth Government.

The majority voted in favour of a [motion](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/debate/?id=2020-10-26.207.4) that the debate be not adjourned. In other words, they voted to continue the debate.

The Recycling and Waste Reduction Charges (Excise) Bill 2020 was moved for a second reading, forming part of the waste export ban charging legislative package. It imposes charges only when considered a duty of excise, with amounts and exemptions to be set in regulations, and does not itself set charge amounts or impose financial impacts.

The speaker moved to rescind the third readings of five recycling and waste reduction bills and to immediately call them on again, with a Minister moving each third reading and the question put without debate.
